title: Correlation immunity from no detected frequency
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let the target be a sign-valued function on $\{-1,1\}^n$, and let $J,P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be coordinate sets. Fix signs on $P$, assume $|J|\le k$, and assume the target depends only on coordinates in $J$. Given a batch of samples indexed by the prescribed sample count, suppose every Fourier estimate in the prescribed low-degree family for the restriction obtained by fixing those signs on $P$ has error strictly less than the prescribed accuracy, and the frequency detector returns none. Then every nonempty Fourier coefficient of that restricted function on a set of size at most $\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: Sign-valued target on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Assignment of signs to coordinates in $P$
Target depends only on coordinates in $J$
Sample batch of the prescribed size
All prescribed low-degree Fourier estimates satisfy the strict accuracy bound
caveat: The formal definitions of the estimate family, detector, and accuracy are omitted from the provided informal definitions; the statement describes their roles and preserves the conclusion.
